Registered Office: 42 Meridian Avenue, Mumbai, Maharashtra, India

Reporting Period: 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026

Aurelia Digital Finance Ltd. (ADFL) is a fictional diversified financial technology company providing digital payments, embedded finance, credit analytics, and financial infrastructure services to banks, merchants, and small businesses. During FY2025–26, the company expanded its institutional customer base while continuing investments in artificial intelligence, cloud infrastructure, information security, and responsible finance.

The company operates through three principal business lines: Digital Payments, Enterprise Credit Intelligence, and Financial Infrastructure Services. Its strategy is centered on increasing recurring enterprise revenue, improving transaction-level risk controls, and developing reusable financial data and AI capabilities.

- Revenue increased by 24.6% compared with FY2024–25.

- Enterprise customers increased from 146 to 219.

- Adjusted EBITDA margin improved from 12.4% to 15.8%.

- Technology and product investment increased by 31.2%.

- The company introduced a formal Responsible AI Governance Framework.

Unless otherwise stated, the financial information in this report covers Aurelia Digital Finance Ltd. and its wholly controlled operating subsidiaries for the year ended 31 March 2026. Sustainability indicators cover the same entities except for selected supplier metrics, which use information available from material suppliers as of 30 June 2026.

FY2025–26 was characterized by sustained revenue growth, improving operating leverage, and increased investment in technology. Revenue reached INR 1,842.6 crore compared with INR 1,478.8 crore in the previous financial year. Profit after tax increased to INR 186.4 crore from INR 131.7 crore. Management attributes the improvement to higher enterprise transaction volumes, improved pricing discipline, and lower customer-acquisition costs in mature markets.

Digital Payments generated INR 928.4 crore of revenue and remained the largest business segment. Enterprise Credit Intelligence generated INR 564.2 crore, supported by increased demand for underwriting analytics and portfolio monitoring. Financial Infrastructure Services generated INR 350.0 crore and recorded the highest year-on-year growth among the three segments.

ADFL's risk management framework is designed to identify, assess, monitor, mitigate, and report risks that may materially affect financial performance, regulatory compliance, customer outcomes, information security, or business continuity. The Board Risk Committee receives quarterly reporting from management and may request additional reviews when risk indicators exceed approved thresholds.

| Risk | Description | Primary Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Credit Risk | Potential loss arising from counterparty or borrower default. | Credit scoring, exposure limits, portfolio monitoring. |
| Cybersecurity Risk | Unauthorized access, data loss, or disruption of critical systems. | MFA, encryption, SOC monitoring, penetration testing. |
| Model Risk | Incorrect outcomes from analytical or AI models. | Validation, monitoring, approval controls, human oversight. |
| Regulatory Risk | Failure to comply with applicable financial-sector requirements. | Compliance testing, regulatory inventory, training. |

section: 3 Risk Management > 3.2 AI and Model Risk
text: The company uses machine-learning models for fraud detection, credit risk assessment, customer segmentation, and operational forecasting. Model owners are required to document intended use, training data, material assumptions, validation results, performance thresholds, known limitations, and escalation procedures. Production models undergo periodic monitoring for drift and material changes in error rates.

section: 3 Risk Management > 3.2 AI and Model Risk
text: Long-form policy clause: Where an automated or AI-assisted decision may materially affect a customer, the responsible business unit must maintain a documented process for review, challenge, escalation, and remediation. No model may be deployed into a material decision workflow without an approved owner, documented validation evidence, defined performance thresholds, and a mechanism for investigating anomalous outcomes. Where monitoring identifies a statistically significant deterioration in performance, material data-quality issues, unexpected distributional changes, or evidence of systematic bias, the model owner must notify the Model Risk Committee and initiate an appropriate review. Depending on severity, the review may require recalibration, temporary restriction of automated decisions, enhanced human review, or suspension of the model until corrective action has been completed and formally approved.

The Audit Committee oversees financial reporting, internal controls, statutory audit, and whistleblower mechanisms. The Risk Committee oversees enterprise risk, cyber risk, model risk, and business continuity. The Nomination and Remuneration Committee reviews senior leadership appointments and compensation structures. The Sustainability Committee reviews climate, social, responsible finance, and stakeholder matters.

Although ADFL operates primarily through technology and financial infrastructure, the company recognizes that data centers, office facilities, employee travel, and purchased goods contribute to its environmental footprint. During FY2025–26, the company increased the proportion of renewable electricity used across controlled facilities and introduced supplier screening criteria covering environmental management practices.

section: 5 Sustainability and ESG > 5.2 Social and Responsible Finance
text:
ADFL's social priorities include financial inclusion, responsible product design, employee development, customer privacy, and fair treatment. The company delivered financial-literacy programs to 18,700 participants during the year and provided scholarships to 240 students pursuing technology and finance education.

The company also maintains a customer grievance mechanism through which complaints may be submitted electronically, by telephone, or through designated relationship managers. Complaints involving suspected discrimination, unauthorized use of customer data, or material financial harm are escalated according to the incident-severity matrix and may require review by compliance and senior management.

section: 5 Sustainability and ESG > 5.3 ESG Data Notes
text: Environmental data is compiled using utility invoices, landlord information, energy provider statements, and internal estimates where primary records are unavailable. Certain Scope 3 categories are not reported because the company is still developing supplier-level data collection procedures. ESG metrics are therefore not directly comparable with every financial institution's disclosures.

The company maintains a regulatory obligations register covering applicable financial, data-protection, cybersecurity, employment, tax, and corporate requirements. Compliance owners are assigned to material obligations and provide periodic certifications to the Chief Compliance Officer.

section: 6 Regulatory and Compliance Disclosures > Customer Data Protection Clause
text: Customer information shall be collected, processed, stored, transferred, and deleted only for authorized purposes and in accordance with applicable law and approved internal policies. Access to customer information must be restricted according to role-based permissions and business necessity. Personnel with privileged access must use approved authentication mechanisms and must not disclose credentials, authentication tokens, encryption keys, or confidential customer information to unauthorized persons. Where a security incident is reasonably suspected, the relevant employee or service provider must promptly report the incident through the designated incident-management channel. The company may restrict, suspend, investigate, or terminate access where required to protect customers, systems, confidential information, or regulatory interests.

Management expects the next financial year to focus on disciplined growth, enterprise customer expansion, platform modernization, and continued investment in artificial intelligence. The company expects demand for automated credit analytics, fraud prevention, and financial workflow infrastructure to remain strong, although competitive intensity, regulatory developments, funding costs, cybersecurity threats, and macroeconomic conditions could affect the pace of growth.

The FY2026–27 operating plan includes investments in cloud infrastructure, model governance, data engineering, security controls, and customer-facing analytics. Management has approved a technology investment envelope of INR 235 crore, of which approximately INR 78 crore is allocated to artificial intelligence and data-platform initiatives.
